newsitem.title: THAILAND: Thai baht firms as central bank intervenes late.
newsitem.headline: Thai baht firms as central bank intervenes late.

text.p: The Thai baht was stronger against the dollar in late afternoon trade following the Bank of Thailand's intervention in the Singapore market in late afternoon trade, dealers said.
The baht rose to 25.580-25.590 against the dollar late from 25.600-25.605 in morning trade. Deals were made as low as 25.610-25.615 in early morning trade.
"The central bank made another intervention at around 2.00-3.00 PM after the first intervention in the morning. This helped push the baht up against the dollar," said one dealer at an European bank.
Senior Bank of Thailand officials declined to comment on the reported intervention.
Dealers said the strong selling of the baht against the dollar was triggered by seasonal year-end dollar demand from by some investors. Speculators jumped on the bandwagon and attacked the baht.
Market players started selling the dollar for baht after the spot dollar/baht rate fell below 25.600, they added.
The heavy buying of the dollar pushed the overnight interbank rate up to 14.50-15.00 percent in late trade from 13.00-13.50 in the morning, dealers said.
"Central bank reserve requirements this week also sparked demand for funds today," said one dealer at a foreign bank.
All commercial banks have to meet the BOT's reserve requirements on the seventh and 22nd of each month.
The dollar/baht swap premium was quoted at 11.00/12.00 satangs per a dollar late, unchanged from the early morning.
The Bank of Thailand fixed the dollar/baht mid-rate at 25.55 versus 25.56 on Monday.
